policy_floor: a broken build or test leg on any supported platform that this change INTRODUCED or newly exposed (docs-suite plugin readme gate)
trigger: any run of plugin_doc_gen.py --check (tests/test_plugin_readmes.py in the meson docs suite, docs-lint CI) after the plugin README 'Where the data goes' edits
classification_rationale: the committed generated manifests still said 'Not consumed by daily-sync' while the README source said the opposite; generator check failed (2 errors) and test_plugin_readmes failed 1 of 15; the manifests are served as data via yuzu://plugin-docs
summary: Generated plugin manifests (pkg_inventory.json, windows_optional_features.json) were not regenerated after the README edits. Found independently by plugin-developer, docs-writer and architect, each by running the generator check read-only; the orchestrator reproduced it. The earlier gates missed it because the docs suite was not in the evidence list. Fixed in 6b39a2170: plugin_doc_gen.py --all after every README edit (installed_apps.json too), --check 0 errors, test_plugin_readmes 15 OK.

trigger: one adapter reads more than 20,001 raw rows and at least one exact duplicate lies among the first 20,001 (for example the Windows 64-bit and WOW6432 hives listing the same package), so the post-dedup merged count falls to 20,000 or fewer
classification_rationale: the plan's cap rule (reject an over-cap host rather than send a truncated list) was implemented only on the post-dedup count; every splitter stops at kMaxEntries + 1 raw rows so the unread tail is dropped silently while the hash still agrees with the server
summary: The over-cap guard could be bypassed when duplicates pull the deduped count under the cap, shipping a truncated inventory as complete with no signal. Reported independently by happy/unhappy-path (native NICE) and architect (native SHOULD); the derived band is HIGH (I3, E5; E6 cannot be claimed). Practical odds negligible (largest measured host 460 records). Fixed in 6b39a2170 by one per-action raw-row guard after row.adapt() (covers every table row, merged check kept), with tests (20,001 raw rows including an exact duplicate skips; 20,000 distinct still sends).

trigger: a std::bad_alloc or std::length_error thrown inside collect() on the sync thread (four adapters up to ~20,001 rows each plus a 3.5 MiB capture)
classification_rationale: the ScopeExit comment says the handle is cleared 'on a throw out of tick()' but an uncaught exception out of a std::thread calls std::terminate; the heartbeat thread has the firewall, the sync thread did not
summary: The daily-sync thread had no exception firewall, so a throw in collect() would terminate the agent. The old single-call collector had the same shape; the multi-action collector widens the allocation exposure. Fixed in 6b39a2170: try/catch(std::exception)+catch(...) around scheduler.tick with a warn and a 60 s retry (interruptible by the stop flag); the Gate 8 code review confirmed no hot spin, consistent persisted state and unchanged join order.

trigger: an operator reading 'a multi-million-endpoint fleet upgrading at once sends every full report together' and staging the upgrade on that basis
classification_rationale: sync_scheduler.cpp persists a per-agent next_slot(..., phase_offset) so the first post-upgrade report lands at each agent's own daily slot; the manual already said 'Spread, not lockstep'; the sentence came from an earlier adversarial-review finding that assumed a lockstep resend
summary: The changelog's rollout sentence contradicted the scheduler. Found independently by docs-writer and the ops reviewer; the orchestrator verified it. The 'no server admission control for inventory resends' half was verified true. Fixed in 6b39a2170: first post-upgrade full report arrives at each agent's phase-spread slot; lockstep only for agents with no persisted state, agents overdue at reconnect, and a fleet-wide Sync now; staging by group advisable for very large fleets, not mandatory. Supersedes the adversarial-review r1 wording.

trigger: an operator upgrades agents and sees a host skip its daily report with a 'skipping this cycle' warning, or reads the manual's upgrade section
classification_rationale: required doc category 2 (docs/user-manual section for a changed operator workflow / upgrade step): the Upgrading paragraph covered the server schema migration only and troubleshooting named only a missing installed_apps plugin
summary: The user manual had no agent-side upgrade note and no troubleshooting entry for the new skip-the-cycle warnings (whole report skipped when DISM is busy or Homebrew is constrained; yuzu_inventory_stale_agents flags after two missed cycles), and its failure list omitted the malformed-status and zero-feature-rows cases. Reported by docs-writer and the ops reviewer. Fixed in 6b39a2170 and a31ad68e2 (also the over-cap warnings).

trigger: a future edit swaps the package_id and source arms of entry_less, or removes the clamp_field calls in the new adapters, then a package id, version or feature name arrives with invalid UTF-8, a framing byte or over 1024 bytes
classification_rationale: the tail-order assertion held under any deterministic comparator and reverting any adapter clamp left every new test green, so the tests could not observe what they claimed; ordinary missing coverage is SHOULD (I8: degraded assurance); the reviewer's native I5/I3 describe the hypothetical regression these tests would catch (a swapped comparator or a removed clamp), which is not itself present in the code
summary: The package_id-vs-source comparator order and the per-adapter clamp were not pinned by a discriminating test. Fixed in 6b39a2170: a pair that disagrees in direction asserted in both input orders; clamp cases per adapter (0x1F in a name, over-length versions, invalid UTF-8); per-source counts 393/66/1; the byte-cap case also asserts the capture is not truncated. The Gate 8 reviewers checked by revert-reasoning that each new test bites; the earlier fixer mutation probe showed the truncation, byte-cap and status-action assertions fail when their guards are removed.

trigger: an MCP or REST client reads the published closed vocabulary (ecosystem ... homebrew, kind package|app) and filters on a value the agent no longer emits (brew, optional_feature, pkg, feat)
classification_rationale: required doc category 1 (REST/MCP reference for a changed body vocabulary): mcp_server.cpp:667 and the rest_api_v1.cpp:1064 OpenAPI literal still list homebrew; editing them is a server change with an MSVC C2026 literal-length hazard and an MCP tool-description contract, so it was routed to a server follow-up (option b) with only the header comments fixed here
summary: Published closed-vocabulary descriptions (MCP tool description, OpenAPI description) and the dormant CPE normalizer (cpe_normalize.hpp:79 compares homebrew, never matches brew) still advertise the old ecosystem values. The agent-side and server-header comments were fixed in 6b39a2170. The two published strings plus cpe_normalize are one server follow-up.

trigger: a SyncPluginMap holding key installed_apps with a null descriptor plus a loaded pkg_inventory that returns rows
classification_rationale: the anchor check tested key presence while the loop skipped a null descriptor; unreachable in production because agent.cpp dereferences the descriptor before emplace, so the wrong outcome (a brew-only blob replacing the stored apps) cannot occur there; only a test-built map could trigger it
summary: The installed_apps anchor guard used contains() but the table loop treats a null descriptor as absent. Fixed in 6b39a2170 with one find() that also requires a non-null descriptor.

trigger: a reader following the SwEntry field comments, the README line cite, the matrix row, the routed-concerns clause or the warn text
classification_rationale: comments that contradict the code (kind/ecosystem/version vocabularies, 'the agent emits package_id/source', '12 fields', '16k rows', stale README line range, matrix row without OS qualifiers, warn text without a verb); wording-only, no behaviour
summary: Stale comments and cross-references after the multi-action collector, reported by cpp-expert, cpp-safety, plugin-developer, docs-writer, architect and quality-engineer. Fixed in 6b39a2170 and a31ad68e2.

trigger: Windows DISM busy/timeout/abandoned or api_unavailable, or a constrained Homebrew walk on macOS: any failing action skips the whole day's report including the installed_apps rows
classification_rationale: accepted by design (the MVP honesty rule: nothing falsely deleted; per-plugin independence is a later roadmap row) and documented in the manual; no skip counter exists although the roadmap row says 'existing counter'; the only operator signal is yuzu_inventory_stale_agents after 48 h
summary: A failing secondary plugin vetoes the whole report; a skip costs a full 24 h and the host is flagged stale after two missed cycles even if healthy. Documented in the manual in this change; per-plugin carry-forward and an agent-side skip counter are follow-up work.

trigger: the Linux pkg_inventory managers leg ships and returns a constrained status for facts the adapter discards
classification_rationale: the managers adapter consumes only presence and version yet a constrained status fails the whole cycle; the constraints come from facts walks it throws away; latent until another leg ships, and no sync-source diff would accompany that change
summary: Latent stall trap: a constrained managers answer skips every host's inventory for rows the adapter drops.

trigger: an action or plugin is renamed, a duplicate plugin descriptor name is loaded, or a non-anchor plugin is absent
classification_rationale: source = <plugin>.<action> is now a stored and hashed value, so renaming an action changes stored source and forces a fleet-wide resend; the collector tests exercise the real names against the real captures so a rename fails the agent suite today; an absent non-anchor plugin deletes its rows silently at debug level; sync_plugins.emplace is first-wins while tar_descriptor and the others are last-wins (the loader does not produce duplicates)
summary: Contract coupling worth recording: stored source value, absent-plugin row deletion at debug level, first-wins versus last-wins descriptor maps.

trigger: MSVC /W3 compile of tests/unit/test_inventory_sync.cpp: C4125 'decimal digit terminates octal escape sequence' on two string literals
classification_rationale: the two literals (inv|na\037me|1\0362|... and A\0371\037P...) are on dev already (lines 241 and 337 at the base); warning only (werror=false), result correct; the same real-MSVC run of this change was otherwise GREEN: [sync] 4069 assertions in 49 cases pass on MSVC 19.44, the three new adapter symbols export, the sample files and YUZU_PLUGIN_SRC_DIR resolve on Windows
summary: Pre-existing MSVC warning on two older test literals, found by the real-MSVC verification of this change on the-rig; not introduced here and not fixed here.
Follow-up filed as #5328 (server: published ecosystem/kind vocabulary and the CPE lane).
Follow-up filed as #5327 (per-action carry-forward and an agent-side skip counter).
Parked as #5329 (roadmap): latent until another managers leg ships; impact I8 only, so parking is allowed.
Follow-up filed as #5330 (pin the action table against the real descriptors; make an absent plugin visible).
Follow-up filed as #5334 (pre-existing octal-escape literals).

trigger: a future inventory action (MSI packages, runtimes, driver inventory) returns rc 0 with partial rows and no in-band status marker
classification_rationale: the collector reads only rc and truncated and ignores the dispatcher's typed result_completeness (agents/core/src/local_dispatcher.hpp:55); every current action carries an in-band guard, so no wrong outcome exists today
summary: No generic partial-result guard for future table actions.

trigger: two consecutive skipped daily cycles on a healthy online host (for example a long Windows DISM abandoned slot)
classification_rationale: yuzu_inventory_stale_agents uses a 2 x 24 h cutoff and cannot tell an offline agent from an online agent whose collector skipped; the manual now documents the behaviour
summary: Stale-agents gauge flags a healthy host after two skipped cycles; needs a skip reason tag.

trigger: start-UAT.sh start on a shared host where another session has a process whose command line contains yuzu-agent or yuzu-server (including a locked build wrapper)
classification_rationale: kill_stale matches by command-line substring across all sessions; observed 2026-10-03 killing a locked meson compile wrapper; not a defect of this diff, recorded so the finding has a disposition
summary: start-UAT.sh kill_stale() kills other sessions' processes including build tooling; follow-up filed.
